title: A doctor for document schemas, and an opt-in pass that makes a project's documents fit
tldr: Every docs-corpus answer is only as good as the frontmatter and the sections of the documents underneath it. Nothing tells a user which of their files the MCP can read and which it skips, and nothing offers to fix the ones it cannot. Two pieces: a **doctor** that reports fitness per file, and an **opt-in skill** that reads a project's features and rewrites their headers to the current schema.
notes: Formerly item 1.4 of docs/backlog/index.md.

**Do this BEFORE 1.2.** 1.2 migrates relationships into a project that declared none; it cannot know what it is walking until something reports which documents are already readable. The doctor is that report, and 1.2 records the same suspension from its own side.

**What made this urgent.** The impact-question delivery of 2026-09-14 deleted the last reader that tolerated an old document shape. From now on a document is either in the current format or it is **invisible to the MCP, silently** — it parses, it lands in the corpus, and it answers nothing. Silence is the defect: an empty answer and an unreadable file look identical from the caller's side, which is the exact confusion `add-knowledge-discovery` already had to be taught to separate.

**The doctor reports, and writes nothing.** For every document in the docs corpus: fit, off-standard, or unreadable, naming the field or section that is missing rather than a score. `add-doc-schemas` owns the schemas, so the doctor reads them from there — a doctor that restates a schema drifts from it, and the drift is invisible until the two disagree about what "fit" means.

**The fix pass is a skill, not a codemod.** It reads each feature's document and adjusts the header — frontmatter `type` and `id`, the `## Relations` block — to the current schema. It has to be an agent reading the content, because deciding a document's type and its relations is a judgement, not a text substitution. Opt-in, and it edits headers only: never a body, never a deletion.

⛔ **The user writes nothing by hand.** Every one of those documents was written by a command, so a migration that hands the user a list of files to edit is addressing the wrong actor. The skill's output is the edit; the user's part is approving it. This is the rule the impact-question build established, and it is what killed the legacy converter there.

**Carried over from the impact-question delivery: the behaviour with no index at all.** `touched_by` answers empty in a project that has never run a close-out. `git log --follow <path>` answers it with no index and no plugin, always. Whatever ships must degrade to that rather than to nothing — and the doctor is where a user finds out which of the two they are getting.

**The open question, and it is why this is recorded and not planned.** Where does the doctor live?
- **An MCP action**, beside `search` and `history` — the agent asks it mid-flow, in the same session it is about to query, and gets the caveat before the answer. Costs an action on a surface that already has eleven.
- **A CLI verb**, `codeadd doctor` — a user runs it once after install, reads a report, and decides. Costs the agent a route it cannot take on its own.
- **Both, over one implementation.** That is already the shape `scripts/graph.js` and `mcp/` hold over one sidecar, asserted identical by test rather than shared by code. It is the likeliest answer and it is still a decision, not a default.
done_when: a project holding a mix of current-format and off-standard documents gets a per-file verdict naming the missing field; the opt-in skill converts an off-standard feature header and the same file then answers a docs-corpus query it did not answer before; no body text is modified and no document is deleted by either piece; and `touched_by` on a project with no index at all returns the documented git answer instead of an empty list.

title: Migration command: initial relationship graph for old installs
tldr: An opt-in command that builds an initial relationship structure over features delivered before the typed-relation format existed, grouped by app/group/category as a tree or graph, so the agent can find correlated features and know what to search.
notes: Formerly item 1.2 of docs/backlog/index.md.

**The relationship format this item migrates INTO is delivered, so nothing blocks this any more.** (It was item 1.1, removed from this backlog on delivery — `git log --follow docs/backlog/index.md` has it.) `2026-09-12T104012-PLAN--docs-knowledge-graph-mcp` shipped the typed `## Relations` section, the closed vocabulary (`caused_by`, `depends_on`, `part_of`, `links_to`) and the docs-corpus MCP that reads them. `templates/related.md` is gone and the `hotfix-related` schema is retired.

**Half of the migration also shipped.** `cli/src/migrations.js` migration 0002 (`harvestRelations`) walks a brownfield project's `docs/`, harvests the relationships it already wrote — body references, `related:` ids, Follow-up sentences — and writes them as `links_to` lines. Additive-only: it never deletes, never commits, and reports every id that resolves to no work item.

**What is left is the project that declared nothing.** 0002 finds nothing in a project whose documents never named each other, and that is the common case for deliveries predating the format. Such a project needs a structure derived from what its deliveries have in common — path overlap, directory, domain — rather than from a declaration nobody made.
Scan past deliveries (`docs/features`, changelogs) and group them — by app, group or category, tree or graph: the shape is still open, and choosing it is the first half of this item.
Ships as an enabled feature, not part of the default flow.
When the gitnexus plugin is enabled, the grouping also points at what to search in gitnexus per group.

**Deliberately deferred past 1.4.** The `add-knowledge-discovery` step this command consults on its first run was repaired on 2026-09-14, and the impact question — where a work item's file set lives, which is half of what this migration would have to write — shipped on 2026-09-14 (`git log --follow docs/backlog/index.md` carries the item it was). What is still missing is 1.4: this migration cannot know what it is walking until something reports which of a project's documents the MCP can already read. The usual "finish everything above before starting" rule is suspended for that reason, and recorded here rather than left as an unexplained skip.
done_when: running the command on a project whose deliveries declare no relationship produces the initial grouped structure with relationships filled, and add.new/add.plan/add.hotfix use it as the investigation entry point.

title: Treat obsolete code and backward compatibility as first-class concerns
tldr: /add.build and /add.hotfix explicitly ask whether the work must preserve backward compatibility; when it does not, they guide the author to propose a migration or cleanup script. /add.done surfaces any dead code the feature left behind before merging.
notes: Formerly item 2.1 of docs/backlog/index.md.
Add a backward-compatibility question to `/add.build` (around STEP 6/8) and `/add.hotfix` (around STEP 7/8), and record the answer in `plan.md` / `about.md` / hotfix `about.md`.
When backward compatibility is **not** required, require a migration or data-cleanup artifact (script, SQL, worker, or explicit manual steps) before the feature/hotfix can be considered complete.
Add a dead-code detection pass to `/add.done` (before merge) that lists unused files, unreachable routes, orphaned exports, or tables/columns left behind by the delivery.
Extend the relevant `add-doc-schemas` (`feature-plan`, `hotfix-about`, `changelog`) to carry the compatibility decision and any attached migration/cleanup artifact.
done_when: a feature that rewrites an existing model produces a `plan.md` entry stating `backward compatibility: no` plus a migration script path, and `/add.done` reports either `dead code: none` or a concrete cleanup candidate list.

title: Sweep the artefacts for text that informs without instructing, and name the rule that keeps it out
tldr: A pass over every command, skill and agent removing passages that explain rather than instruct, plus a named rule in `building-commands` so the next author recognises the shape before writing it.
notes: Formerly item 3.1 of docs/backlog/index.md.

The rule already half exists: `.claude/skills/building-commands/SKILL.md:583` carries ruler item 7 ("No filler"), and `@prompt-review-agent` ticks it. What it lacks is the concrete shapes to look for — the abstract test "does this change what the executor does" did not stop four instances being written into one delivery and shipped past a five-auditor review.

Name the recurring shapes in item 7, each with an Expected / Not expected pair like the other items carry: telling artefact A how artefact B behaves when nothing in A branches on it; restating a rule already stated a few lines above in different words; explaining the mechanism behind a change, which belongs in the changelog and the commit message because a human reads those once and an agent reads the prompt every run.

Keep the distinction the ruler already draws, so the sweep does not strip what is load-bearing: a scope statement (which commands a section covers, which phase an exemption applies to) and a prohibition restated at the exact point where skipping it is tempting both change what the reader does. Only the passages that survive removal without changing any action come out.

Sweep 106 artefacts: 16 commands, 43 skills and 22 agents under `framwork/.codeadd/`, plus 7 commands, 10 skills and 8 agents under `.claude/`. Product artefacts ship to users and are read on every run, so they pay the token cost repeatedly.

Decide whether anything mechanical can back the rule. Nothing in `cli/tests/` or `scripts/` enforces item 7 today, and a text heuristic for "informs without instructing" may not exist — if it does not, say so in the plan rather than shipping a gate that misses.
done_when: ruler item 7 names the shapes with examples, a run of `@prompt-review-agent` over a deliberately padded artefact flags them by shape rather than by feel, and the sweep's diff shows every artefact it touched with the removed passages listed per file.

title: Board statuses that follow the pipeline phases — from backlog to done
tldr: Replace the four generic statuses (open, doing, done, dropped) with statuses that mirror the pipeline, so a glance at the board says which phase each ticket is in and which command moves it next.
notes: **The user's first sketch.** brainstorm → backlog; add.new → refining → ready for development; add.plan → planning; add.development → doing → ready; add.done → done. There is no `add.development` — the build command is `add.build`.

**Today only two commands write a status.** `add.build` STEP 2 writes `doing` + `work_id` in one write, and `add.done` closes. `add.brainstorm`, `add.new` and `add.plan` read the ticket and write nothing — the `Writes the board?` column of `add-backlog/references/lifecycle.md` says `no` for all three. Every new phase status means one more command writes the board, so that column changes.

**Suggested sequence (to decide in the brainstorm):** `backlog` (captured, nobody picked it up) → `refining` (add.brainstorm or add.new running) → `ready-to-plan` (about.md exists) → `planning` (add.plan running) → `ready-to-build` (plan approved) → `building` (add.build) → `in-review` (build finished, PR open, add.review) → `done` (add.done), plus `dropped` off the flow.

**Suggestion — brainstorm is refining, not backlog.** A ticket reaches brainstorm already on the board, so `backlog` is the state before any command touched it. Brainstorm and add.new are the same phase from the ticket's point of view: shaping what the work is.

**Suggestion — the user's "Ready" after Doing reads as "built, waiting to close".** Name it `in-review`: the PR is open, add.review runs there, and add.done is what leaves it. A column named `ready` twice (ready for development, ready after doing) is ambiguous on the board.

**Suggestion — decide whether the wait states are columns.** Nine columns is a wide kanban. Alternative: one column per phase (backlog, refining, planning, building, review, done) and the waiting part as a badge on the card, e.g. `planning · waiting`. Fewer columns, same information.

**Suggestion — the hotfix path skips phases.** `add.hotfix` goes from a ticket straight to building with no about.md and no plan. The status set must allow a jump, and nothing may refuse a status because the previous one was skipped.

**Suggestion — every status write stays declared, never inferred, and never a stop.** The rule in lifecycle.md holds: a command writes only for the id a `ticket:` field names; a refused or degraded write is one line in the report, exactly as add.build does today.

**Compatibility trap.** `backlog.sh` writes `docs/backlog.definitions.json` once and never rewrites it — it holds user customisation. An existing install keeps `open/doing/done/dropped` forever, and a command writing `planning` there gets `REFUSED=unknown-status`. Needs either a migration in `cli/src/migrations.js`, or commands that fall back when the status is not defined. Renaming `open` also breaks every ticket already on disk, so `backlog` may stay spelled `open` with a new label.

**The internal pipeline follows the same map.** `add-plan-authoring` writes `doing` from `add-framework--build` for this repository's own board; `add-framework--brainstorm`, `--plan` and `--done` get the same rows as their product counterparts.

**The board app needs no column code.** `board/src/lib/tickets.ts` `groupByStatus` already builds one column per defined status in `order`. What it may need is the badge (if wait states are not columns) and hiding `dropped` by default.
done_when: a ticket named by `ticket:` moves through every phase status as add.brainstorm/add.new, add.plan, add.build, the PR and add.done run, each move one board write; the board shows it in the matching column at each step; a project with the old four-status definitions file either migrates or reports the missing status without stopping the command; and add.hotfix can take a ticket straight to building.

title: Add ZCode (Z.ai) as a sixth provider
tldr: Ship commands, skills and agents to ZCode, Z.ai's free agentic desktop IDE for GLM models, so a user running it gets the same framework as Claude Code or Codex. ZCode is close to Claude Code in layout and tool names; the one real blocker is that it refuses command names containing a dot.
notes: **Research done on 2026-09-23, from the official docs (zcode.z.ai/en/docs) AND the open source (github.com/zai-org/ZCode, main branch).** Where they disagree, the source wins and the disagreement is noted. Source files worth re-reading if a detail is doubted: `apps/zcode-cli/packages/adapters/src/commands/{index,roots}.ts`, `packages/services/src/skills/skillsService.ts`, `apps/zcode-cli/packages/bootstrap/src/subagents.ts`, `apps/zcode-cli/packages/adapters/src/context/index.ts`, `apps/zcode-cli/packages/core/src/subagent/profile.ts`.

**Instructions — AGENTS.md works.** It walks up from the working directory to the git root and uses the FIRST `AGENTS.md` it finds (no merging across levels), prepended by the global `~/.zcode/AGENTS.md`. It does NOT read `CLAUDE.md` (the docs say so explicitly). `/init` also looks for `.zcode/AGENTS.md` and `.agents/AGENTS.md`.

**Commands.** Project roots: `.zcode/commands/*.md` AND `.agents/commands/*.md`, scanned at every level from cwd up to the git root, `.zcode` first; on a name clash the first found wins. Global: `~/.zcode/commands/`. Frontmatter keys accepted: `description`, `argument-hint`, `allowed-tools`, `model`, `skills`, `disable-noninteractive` (an unknown key is a warning, not a drop). Body placeholder: `$ARGUMENTS`. Invoked as `/name`. A subdirectory becomes `:` in the name — `commands/add/plan.md` is `/add:plan`.

⛔ **THE BLOCKER — a dot is not a legal command name.** `COMMAND_NAME_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_:-]{0,63}$/` in `adapters/src/commands/index.ts`. `add.plan.md` normalises to `add.plan`, fails the pattern with `custom_command_invalid_name` (severity error) and the command does not load. Every product command except `add` has a dot. Three routes, and choosing one is the first decision of the plan: **(a)** emit `commands/add/plan.md` → `/add:plan`, and have the build rewrite `/add.plan` references to `/add:plan` in the ZCode output only, or every handoff points at a command that does not exist; **(b)** emit `add-plan.md` → `/add-plan`, same text-rewrite problem; **(c)** ship commands as skills, as codex and antigrav already do (`commands: "skills/{name}/SKILL.md"`) — but whether a SKILL `name` may contain a dot is NOT verified: no skill-name pattern was found in the source, so test it on a real install before choosing (c).

**Skills.** Project roots: `.zcode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` AND `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` — the runtime MERGES both (not a fallback). Global: `~/.zcode/skills/`. `name` and `description` are required; missing either drops the skill. `description` over 1024 chars drops the whole skill. Body truncated above 100KB. Invoked as `$name` or from the `/` menu. Only name + a 250-char description excerpt go into context per turn; the body loads on use. The scan descends into subdirectories (so `references/` is fine) but skips dot-directories and `node_modules`, `dist`, `build` and the like.

⚠️ **Double-listing risk with Codex.** The codex provider installs to `.agents/` (`cli/src/providers.js`), and ZCode reads `.agents/skills` and `.agents/commands` too. A user with both codex and zcode installed sees every skill twice if zcode also writes `.zcode/skills`. One option to weigh: zcode installs NO skills of its own and relies on `.agents/skills`, or the installer detects codex and skips the duplicate. Decide in the plan.

**Agents (subagents).** Format is Markdown with YAML frontmatter, body = system prompt — nearly the Claude dialect. Keys: `name`, `description` (required), `model` (a model id or `inherit`), `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `skills`, `maxTurns`, `color`, `thoughtLevel` (only with an explicit model), `injectAgentsMd` (default true), `mcpServers`. Tool names are Claude Code's: `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Bash`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `TodoWrite`, `NotebookEdit`, `Agent`, `Skill`, `AskUserQuestion`, `EnterPlanMode`, `Workflow`, `Task*`, `Cron*`. Reserved names: `general-purpose`, `Explore`. A subagent cannot spawn another. Dispatch: automatic by description, or `@name`.

⚠️ **Docs vs source on project agents.** The docs say subagents are user-level only. The source (`bootstrap/src/subagents.ts`) already loads `<cwd>/.zcode/agents/*.md` as `source: project`, stripping `permissionMode` from project files for safety. So project agents depend on the ZCode version: record a minimum version in the provider's docs, or install agents globally (`~/.zcode/agents/`) as a fallback.

**Agent dialect for `scripts/build.js` `AGENT_DIALECTS`.** Start from the `claude` dialect — same keys, same tool names, so `readonly` → `disallowedTools: Write, Edit, NotebookEdit` works as is. The one difference: `model` values like `sonnet`/`opus` are not ZCode model ids — map them to `inherit` or drop the key. The build throws if a provider has an `agents` pattern and no dialect, so this dialect is mandatory, not optional.

**MCP.** Project: `<root>/.zcode/config.json`, key `mcp.servers` (`{command, args, env}` for stdio; HTTP and SSE also supported). Global: `~/.zcode/cli/config.json`. It imports from Claude, Codex and OpenCode configs. Needed for `cli/src/mcp-registration.js` (the artefact-graph/knowledge MCP registration table has one row per provider) and for the plugin checks (gitnexus, playwright).

**Hooks — project hooks do NOT run.** The docs state it: hooks in `<workspace>/.zcode/config.json` or `<workspace>/zcode.json` are ignored in the current version. Only global `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` with `hooks.enabled: true` runs them. Event names match Claude's (`SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `Stop`). So `capabilities.hooks` is `false` for a project install.

**Plugins — an alternative distribution route worth a look, not a requirement.** A ZCode plugin bundles commands, skills, agents, `hooks/hooks.json` and `.mcp.json`. Manifest lookup: `.zcode-plugin/plugin.json`, then `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — a Claude Code plugin loads unchanged. Plugin hooks DO run, unlike project hooks.

**Proposed `framwork/provider-map.json` entry (starting point, the command path depends on the blocker decision):** `"zcode": { "dir": "framwork/.zcode", "commands": "commands/{name}.md", "skills": "skills/{name}/SKILL.md", "agents": "agents/{name}.md", "capabilities": { "hooks": false, "agentDispatch": true, "mcp": true, "nativeFormat": "md", "slashCommands": true, "structuredQuestions": true }, "docs": ["https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/commands", "https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/skill", "https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/subagents", "https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/mcp-services", "https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/hooks"] }`. `structuredQuestions: true` because `AskUserQuestion` exists.

**Where a new provider is wired in this repo (found by grep, 2026-09-23):** `framwork/provider-map.json` (registry), `scripts/build.js` (`AGENT_DIALECTS`, and the output dir list), `cli/src/providers.js` (`PROVIDERS` entry with src/dest/commandsSubdir/skillsSubdir/agentsSubdir/globalDest, plus `PROVIDER_PRIORITY`), `cli/src/mcp-registration.js` (one row per provider: file + format), `cli/src/uninstaller.js` (`ADD_DIRS` / `GLOBAL_ADD_DIRS` must learn `.zcode`), `workbench/skills/add-framework-product-layer/SKILL.md` (names the providers). The "5 providers" wording in `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` and the web docs also changes — `add-framework--sync` regenerates the last two.

**Feature injection and plugin agent injection.** Commands are markdown with `<!-- feature: -->` markers, so `commandsSubdir: 'commands'` lets feature injection work if route (a) or (b) is chosen. If route (a) nests commands in `add/`, check that `cli/src/injection-core.js` finds files one level down. `agentInjection` stays Claude-only today; ZCode could take it later since its agents are markdown.
**Global install.** ZCode has a real global root (`~/.zcode/{commands,skills,agents,AGENTS.md}`), so `globalDest: '.zcode'` is possible — unlike cursor and antigrav.
done_when: `npm run build` emits `framwork/.zcode/` with every command, skill and agent; installing with the zcode provider into a scratch project and opening it in ZCode lists every framework command under `/` (none dropped with `custom_command_invalid_name`), every skill under `$`, and every agent under `@`; a handoff line inside a command names a command that actually exists in that install; a project with codex and zcode both installed does not list any skill twice; the cli test suite covers the new provider entry and agent dialect; and uninstall removes `.zcode/`.

title: Feature enable order changes the bytes of the installed add.plan
tldr: Enabling tdd-pipeline and qa-pipeline in different orders produces different add.plan files; the installed command should not depend on the order features were switched on.
notes: **Found during delivery 0005B, reproduced without the board feature.** tdd-pipeline and qa-pipeline anchor their step-list sections on the SAME anchor line of add.plan: the two marker pairs sit back to back at framwork/.codeadd/commands/add.plan.md:99-102, right after "- 7.4: Frontend Specialist". Whichever feature is enabled LAST lands FIRST.

**Observed:** enable tdd>qa>docs versus the reverse order swaps "STEP 9.0: QA-Spec subagent" and "STEP 8: Test-Spec subagent". STEP 8 (tdd) should always read before STEP 9.0 (qa), whatever the order.

**Why the suite misses it:** injection-exclusivity.integration.test.js:462, "reversed enable order still lands every full block exactly once", asserts that every block landed, never that the bytes match between the two orders.

**Where the fix likely lives:** cli/src/injection-core.js groups sibling sections by anchor (groupPointsByAnchor, line 160) and applies them bottom-up (applyInjectionToContent, line 180). Sections of DIFFERENT features sharing one anchor need a deterministic order that does not depend on which was already in the file.
**board-feature.test.js L6.4 works around it on purpose:** it keeps the other features in one fixed order so it tests the board feature alone, and says why in a comment. Widen it once this is fixed.
done_when: Enabling tdd-pipeline and qa-pipeline in either order produces a byte-identical add.plan with the tdd step before the qa step, and a test asserts byte equality between the two orders rather than only that every block landed.

title: Pass long scripts and multi-line bodies through a file, never an inline heredoc
tldr: Agents write a long script, JSON record or PR body to a scratch file with the Write tool and run or pass that file, instead of embedding it in a Bash heredoc that breaks on quotes, backslashes and backticks.
notes: Seen on 2026-09-24 while editing board/e2e/board.spec.ts: a ~120-line python edit script passed as cat <<'EOF' | python failed with: unexpected EOF while looking for matching quote (line 125). The same content, saved with the Write tool to the scratchpad and run as python <file>, worked on the first try.

It keeps happening: long inline scripts carrying regexes with backslashes, nested single and double quotes, template literals with ${} and backticks. The root cause inside the Bash tool was not verified; the file route sidesteps it whatever the cause is.
The framework itself prescribes the fragile pattern: framwork/.codeadd/commands/add.pull-request.md builds the PR body with gh pr create --body "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)" and gh pr edit the same way.

backlog-commit.sh takes its record as printf '%s' '<record>' in single quotes, so any apostrophe in a title or note breaks the call. Its usage already accepts stdin, so < file works with no script change.
Same shape as the gh pr edit workaround already in use: gh api ... -F body=@file.

Proposed rule: above a few lines, or with any quote, backslash, backtick or ${} inside, write the content to a scratch file with Write and pass the path (python file.py, node file.mjs, --body-file, -F body=@file, < record.json). Temp files go in the session scratchpad.
done_when: A rule in the workbench authoring skill and in the product commands that pass multi-line content tells the agent to write it to a file and pass the path; grep -rn "<<'EOF'" framwork/.codeadd workbench returns no instruction that inlines a multi-line body; add.pull-request.md uses --body-file.

title: Evaluate removing the dot from command names (add.plan -> add-plan or add:plan)
tldr: ZCode (0006B) exposed that the dot in command names (add.plan, add.build...) is a hard incompatibility with at least one provider and is worth reconsidering framework-wide, separately from the ZCode delivery which resolves it locally by reusing codex output.
notes: Raised while planning 0006B (ZCode as sixth provider). The dot convention is canonical today: 14 product commands, all named add.<verb>, declared in framwork/provider-map.json and enforced/described by add-id-convention and add-resource-path-convention.
0006B does NOT rename anything — it ships zcode by reusing codex's existing command-as-skill output (framwork/.agents), sidestepping the naming question for that one provider.

A rename here means every command file, every {{cmd:}} reference, every literal /add.plan mention in skills/docs (e.g. add-ecosystem's routing table), README, web docs, and breaks muscle memory for existing installs. Needs its own brainstorm before any plan.
Candidate target shapes: add-plan (dash, matches skill naming) or add:plan (colon, native ZCode subdirectory convention) — trade-offs undecided.
done_when: A brainstorm exists deciding whether to rename product commands off the dot, and to what shape, or explicitly closes as not-worth-it.

title: Avaliar o GitNexus para o desenvolvimento do board, e estender os comandos internos se valer a pena
tldr: GitNexus indexa um repo e responde perguntas estruturais (call graph, blast-radius, trace de fluxo) via MCP. board/src ja e um app React/TS real (components, hooks, routes, views, lib, api), entao ha uso genuino: 'o que quebra se eu mudar este hook', 'traca esse fluxo de api ate o componente'. Falta decidir se isso justifica indexar board/ e ajustar os comandos internos, ou se os skills gitnexus-* nativos (gitnexus-exploring, gitnexus-impact-analysis, gitnexus-refactoring) ja bastam sem mudanca nenhuma.
notes: Pedido do usuario: usar gitnexus no board para ajudar no desenvolvimento, e se fizer sentido, ajustar os comandos internos (framework) tambem.

Hoje o plugin gitnexus so injeta fragments nos comandos do produto (add.build, add.plan, add.new, add.diagnose, add.done, add.hotfix, add.wiki) e nos agentes de product-layer (frontend-agent etc.) — framwork/.codeadd/plugins/gitnexus/fragments/. Nenhum deles opera sobre board/, que e um diretorio de produto na raiz do repo, fora do pipeline add.* e fora do workbench.

Os skills nativos gitnexus-* (gitnexus-exploring, gitnexus-debugging, gitnexus-impact-analysis, gitnexus-refactoring, gitnexus-pr-review, gitnexus-cli) nao sao amarrados a nenhum comando ADD — funcionam standalone assim que o repo estiver indexado (gitnexus-cli: 'Index this repo'). Ou seja, dar suporte ao board pode nao precisar de nenhum ajuste em comando: basta indexar board/ como repo e usar os skills nativos direto durante o desenvolvimento.

Ajustar comando interno so faz sentido se quisermos que add-framework--build/add-framework--plan (workbench/) dispatchem gitnexus automaticamente quando um F-block toca board/ — hoje esse dispatch so existe para framwork/.codeadd/ e cli/ (product layer) e para workbench/ (internal layer), sem nada especifico para board/.

Decisao pendente antes de programar algo: (1) indexar board/ com gitnexus-cli e testar uso manual dos skills nativos por algumas sessoes reais de desenvolvimento do board; (2) só depois, se o ganho for claro, decidir se vale criar um fragment/agent hook proprio para board/ nos comandos internos, ou se e overkill para um app desse tamanho.
done_when: board/ indexado no gitnexus (gitnexus-cli status confirma), e uma decisao registrada (aqui mesmo, via comment) sobre se os comandos internos precisam de ajuste ou se os skills nativos gitnexus-* bastam como estao.

title: Turn the `add` gateway into `add-help`, a help guide for how the framework works
tldr: Rename the bare `add` command to `add--help` and make it a help guide: it explains how the framework works and answers questions like how to enable QA, and what GitNexus is and how to enable it.
notes: Formerly the rename-only ticket. Decided by Maicon on 2026-10-09: the rename to `add--help` stays, because the name tells the user what the command is. The naming question is closed: the name is `add--help`.

New focus (2026-10-09): the command becomes a help guide. It explains how the framework works and answers questions such as how to enable QA (the `qa-pipeline` feature) and what GitNexus is and how to enable it (the `gitnexus` plugin). If needed, refactor `add.md` for this purpose.
The artefact is the product command `framwork/.codeadd/commands/add.md`, titled "ADD - Intelligent Ecosystem Gateway". It is read-only for project code.
Registered under the key `"add"` in `framwork/provider-map.json` (first entry of the `commands` object).

Named in `framwork/.codeadd/skills/add-ecosystem/SKILL.md`: line 3 ("Loaded by /add as source of truth") and line 75 (`- mention: /add`). That skill is the source the command loads, so the rename has to move both.

Answers about enabling features and plugins come from `cli/src/features.js` (toggled with `codeadd features enable|disable <name>`), `cli/src/plugins.json`, `framwork/.codeadd/fragments/qa-pipeline` and `framwork/.codeadd/plugins/gitnexus`. The help guide must read from these sources instead of hard-coding steps that drift.

A rename is wider than the file: every `/add` mention, the ecosystem map, provider output, and the docs `add-framework--sync` regenerates (README, web docs) must move in the same delivery, or a handoff points at a command that no longer exists.
Adjacent to, but distinct from, 0010B (removing the dot from `add.plan`). `add` carries no dot, so 0010B does not cover it.
done_when: `npm run build` emits the gateway as `add-help` and no provider output still holds a command named `add`; `/add-help` explains how the framework works and correctly answers 'how do I enable QA' and 'what is GitNexus and how do I enable it'; a grep for a bare `/add` reference across `framwork/.codeadd/`, README and web docs returns none; and an install that had the old `add` command has no dangling reference to it.

title: Deterministic feature docs, read and written through one surface the board and the commands share
tldr: Estudar como melhorar o padrao atual dos *.md de feature para leitura deterministica, exibir isso no board, e expor um API/MCP (ou algo parecido) para os commands, skills e agents buscarem, lerem e salvarem informacoes de feature — a base para, no futuro, o board virar um harness com agentes que fazem toda a gestao e execucao das atividades.
notes: Pedido do usuario: estudar o padrao hoje usado nos *.md das features para serem lidos de forma deterministica, incluir isso na exibicao do board, e incluir API ou MCP para o framework (commands, skills, agents) usar esse mecanismo para buscar, ler e salvar informacoes de feature. Objetivo futuro: transformar o board numa especie de harness com agentes para toda a gestao e execucao de atividades.

Estado atual, verificado: os docs de feature sao markdown de prosa com secoes livres — `framwork/.codeadd/templates/feature-about-template.md` (## Objective, ## Business Context, ## Scope, ## Business Rules...) e `feature-discovery-template.md`. Existe um schema de notacao em `framwork/.codeadd/skills/add-doc-schemas/references/new-feature.md` (IDs estaveis RF/RNF/RN, tabela de decisao, notacao de escopo), mas o arquivo em si nao carrega frontmatter tipado como os docs do docs-corpus. Nada garante que duas execucoes leiam o mesmo documento do mesmo jeito.

O mecanismo ja existe e foi feito para crescer: `mcp/corpora.mjs` e uma tabela declarativa com duas linhas (artefacts, docs) e diz no proprio cabecalho que 'a third corpus later is a row here, not a redesign'. Um corpus `features` e a rota mais provavel — mas decidir entre MCP (o agente consulta mid-flow), API do board (a UI le), ou as duas sobre uma implementacao so, como `scripts/graph.js` e `mcp/` fazem sobre um sidecar, e a primeira metade do estudo.

O board ja reservou o lugar: `board/server.mjs` e read-only, zero-dependency, serve `/api/board` e nunca parseia `docs/backlog.jsonl` (tickets vem de `backlog.sh list --all`). O cabecalho diz 'RESERVED, NOT IMPLEMENTED: /api/runs, /api/runs/:id, /api/tickets/:id/refine' — o harness de agentes e o futuro que o proprio arquivo ja nomeia.

Padrao deterministico provavelmente significa frontmatter tipado (id, feature id, status, relacoes) + secoes com marcadores estaveis, no mesmo espirito do docs-corpus (frontmatter `id:`/`type:` e bloco `## Relations` com vocabulario fechado). Decidir se o alvo e o docs-corpus existente ganhando um tipo `feature` ou um corpus separado: a regra de `corpora.mjs` e que dois corpora nunca compartilham indice nem namespace de node.

Relacao com 0001B (doctor de schemas + passe opt-in que ajusta headers): aquele e sobre o docs-corpus dizer quais documentos ele consegue ler; este e sobre os documentos de feature carregarem estrutura suficiente para o board exibir e para os comandos escreverem de volta. Faz sentido 0001B vir antes como fundacao, mas nao bloqueia o estudo.

Escrita e escopo novo: hoje nenhum caminho do board escreve em feature docs, e o framework escreve via add.new/add.plan. A superficie de leitura/escrita precisa de um caminho de save declarado — quem escreve, para onde, e como reverter — com o mesmo cuidado de host/seguranca que o board ja aplica (127.0.0.1, checagem de Host).

Sem urgencia e sem plano ainda: e estudo. A saida e um brainstorm decidindo (a) o formato deterministico, (b) MCP vs API vs os dois, e (c) o vocabulario de estado de feature que os agentes do harness vao dirigir.
done_when: Um brainstorm registrado decide o formato deterministico dos *.md de feature (frontmatter + secoes estaveis, com um exemplo que um parser le sem fallback), a superficie unica de leitura e escrita (MCP, API do board, ou as duas sobre uma implementacao so), e o vocabulario de estado de feature; e uma prova ponta a ponta mostra um command lendo ou salvando um fato de feature por essa superficie e o board exibindo o mesmo fato a partir do mesmo documento.

title: Fallback de fragmento: preencher o slot quando nenhuma feature ou plugin o ocupa
tldr: Hoje, se a feature que injeta um fragmento esta desligada, o anchor fica vazio e mudo. Um fallback por grupo passaria a preencher esse slot quando nenhum membro do grupo esta habilitado, podendo ser vazio para deixar explicito que o vazio e a resposta.
notes: Pedido do usuario: aperfeicoar a injecao dinamica de fragmentos (features, plugins) com um fallback. Se nada de um determinado grupo preenche um fragmento, o fallback entra no contexto; o fallback pode ser vazio tambem.
ATENCAO: o usuario disse que eram DUAS funcionalidades, mas esqueceu a segunda. Este ticket registra so a primeira (fallback). A segunda entra depois por comment/update, quando ele lembrar.

Como funciona hoje: framwork/.codeadd/commands/*.md carrega marcadores <!-- feature:NAME:SECTION --> e <!-- plugin:NAME:SECTION --> (ex.: add-plan.md:99-102 tem qa-pipeline e tdd-pipeline no MESMO anchor). O build (scripts/build.js, extractInjectionPoints, linha 199) transforma cada marcador aberto num ponto do sidecar framwork/.codeadd/injection-points.json (namespace, name, section, resource, anchor com text/ordinal/position/next) e apaga os marcadores. O arquivo instalado sai sem marcador.

Na instalacao: cli/src/injection-core.js applyInjectionToContent (linha 214) filtra points por sections.has(p.section) e so injeta a secao que existe no fragmento carregado. Se a feature esta off, o fragmento nao e carregado (registry cli/src/features.js FEATURES, e cli/src/plugins.json para plugins), entao NADA e injetado naquele anchor. Nao existe hoje nocao de grupo nem de fallback.

O que falta decidir e implementar: (a) como declarar o grupo e o fallback, um marcador novo (por ex. <!-- fallback:GROUP:SECTION -->) ou o mesmo namespace com uma tabela de grupos no registry; (b) quem resolve o fallback, o build (emite o ponto ja resolvido) ou a CLI na instalacao (so ela conhece o estado habilitado); (c) fallback vazio significa pular o anchor, nao injetar linha em branco; (d) vale para plugin tambem ou so para feature.

A ordem de injecao tem armadilha conhecida quando duas features dividem um anchor (ver 0007B). O fallback precisa respeitar a mesma ordem deterministica para nao depender de qual feature foi ligada por ultimo.
Fonte do fragmento: framwork/.codeadd/fragments/ (features) e framwork/.codeadd/plugins/*/fragments/ (plugins). Um fallback provavelmente mora ao lado, por ex. fragments/<grupo>/fallback.md.

Superficies afetadas: build (scripts/build.js), aplicacao e remocao (cli/src/injection-core.js), registries (cli/src/features.js, cli/src/plugins.json) e os testes de injection (cli/tests/injection-core.test.js, injection-exclusivity.integration.test.js, build-injection-points.test.js).
done_when: Um grupo de features/plugins com todos os membros desligados faz o comando instalado receber o fragmento de fallback no anchor; ligar qualquer membro do grupo suprime o fallback; fallback vazio deixa o anchor intacto, sem linha em branco; e um teste em cli/tests cobre os tres casos.

comments.content:
FECHADO (2026-10-06) — as tres clausulas do done_when verificadas na arvore mesclada (PR #105, merge c64bead; entrega 2026-10-05T152826-PLAN--native-node-framework-scripts).

O MECANISMO. A gramática `<!-- slot:<id> fallback="fallbacks/<arquivo>" -->` substituiu o par de marcadores, e `cli/src/injection-core.js:388-389` resolve o slot: `parts.length ? parts.join('') : (slot.fallback || '')`, com `usedFallback: parts.length === 0`. Um membro que contribui suprime o fallback por construcao — nao por guarda.

OS DOIS FALLBACKS. `framwork/.codeadd/fallbacks/plan-specs.md` (92 bytes, a unica linha aprovada para o step-list compartilhado do add-plan) e `framwork/.codeadd/fallbacks/empty.md` (0 bytes). O fallback vazio e o caso exigido pelo ticket: o anchor fica intacto, sem linha em branco.

O QUE ESTE TICKET NAO FEZ. Nao renomeou nada e nao tocou no registro de backlog: e a mesma entrega que fechou 0007B, e as duas se apoiam no mesmo sidecar v2.

title: Internal PR review with actionable findings and before/after commit evidence
tldr: Create or extend an internal PR review workflow that records actionable findings in a durable checklist, pins the reviewed commit SHA, and links each fix to its own commit SHA and file:line evidence before marking it resolved.
notes: Request arose from reviewing PR #96: the actionable review was written separately, while the internal build review records a single REVIEW line and rulings in the ledger. Define how the new PR-facing document and the existing one-pass delivery review coexist without a second opinion or a stale verdict becoming a gate.

Bounded project check: workbench/commands/ currently contains add-framework--backlog, --release and --sync, but no dedicated internal PR-review command. workbench/skills/add-framework--build/SKILL.md STEP 7 runs a once-only read-only audit, applies accepted findings in the same run and explicitly forbids a review companion; add-review-discipline/SKILL.md also sends durable decisions to the ledger. Decide in design whether to add an internal command or extend that flow, and update the owning rule rather than bypassing it.

A review starts with a recorded checkpoint: PR URL/number, base ref, reviewed head SHA and diff range. Each finding has stable ID, severity, observable symptom, source evidence (file:line at the reviewed SHA), required change, a concrete verification check and a checklist state. Review must be read-only for code.

Fix follow-up retains the original finding and reviewed SHA. For each accepted finding, record the fix commit SHA, the corrected file:line at that SHA, and test/check evidence; mark resolved only when the correction is verified against the updated PR head. A rejected finding records reason instead of a fake fix SHA. Distinguish new code or a force-changed head from the review's pinned snapshot.

The document must make open work easy to route: list unresolved IDs, owners or route to the build, and completion criteria. Evaluate whether the existing ledger records a pointer and checkpoint while the document carries the checklist, or whether one structured record can serve both. Do not duplicate a stale review verdict as a merge gate.

Existing product precedent is framwork/.codeadd/commands/add-review.md (versioned review-NNN.md with ## Fix Routing consumed by add-build), but this request is INTERNAL only; do not copy product feature-specific schema blindly. Register a new workbench command in workbench/provider-map.json only if a new command is chosen.
done_when: Given an open PR with at least two findings, the internal review records its base and reviewed head SHA, writes a document with stable finding IDs, file:line evidence and unchecked actionable fixes; after separate fix commits, each resolved row records its fix SHA, corrected file:line and passing verification at the new head, while an unresolved row remains unchecked; changing the PR head invalidates a stale clean verdict; the review itself changes no application code and the existing one-pass build review/ledger rules have a documented coherent handoff.

comments.content: Dropped by Maicon on 2026-10-09 (board review): more ceremony in the internal pipeline. The done gates, the test-loss guard and CI already cover most of it.

title: Make internal plans verifiable contracts and block incomplete delivery before PR
tldr: Make internal planning map every required outcome to an observable check and proof, then make the build refuse publication when a mandatory check, removal or review is missing, even if a ruling records a deviation.
notes: Separate from 0015B: that ticket covers a durable PR review document and before/after fix evidence. This ticket closes the earlier gap, while the plan is written and before the build publishes. PR #96 showed a plan that already named full STEP-ID migration, v1 removal and final review; the executor recorded rulings for omissions and still opened a PR.

Current owner: workbench/skills/add-plan-authoring/references/plan-template.md requires an Impact map, RED-first Validation Matrix, F-block coverage and reviewer handoff; it does not require a machine-checkable requirement-to-proof map or explicit negative checks for things that must be absent at the final state.

workbench/skills/add-framework--plan/SKILL.md STEP 5 writes the plan and STEP 6 reviews it. Extend the authoring/review contract so every mandatory outcome has a stable ID, source decision, expected end state, test or deterministic check, evidence location, responsible F-block and publish gate. Require an explicit list of things that must disappear (legacy branch, old identifier, obsolete route) when a migration replaces them. Do not mistake passing existing tests for proof of an uncovered requirement.

workbench/skills/add-framework--build/SKILL.md STEP 6 validates per F-block and STEP 7 audits once, but STEP 9's first-push question currently checks the PR state, not whether every plan requirement has passing evidence. Evaluate a mechanical completeness gate before STEP 9, including an already-open PR push: compare plan requirement IDs with tests/check results and current HEAD, fail closed on missing, skipped, stale or unverified items, and do not ask to publish an incomplete delivery.

workbench/skills/add-build-ledger/SKILL.md has F<n>: complete, Ruling, GRAPH and REVIEW line shapes. A Ruling records a decision or cost; it must never silently turn a mandatory plan requirement into optional scope. A scope change requires an explicit user decision and plan revision, followed by updated validation, not a ledger line used as a waiver.

Keep the boundary with 0015B: review findings/checklist and their fix SHAs can be an input to the publish gate, but this ticket should not duplicate the PR review document or dispatch the one-pass adversarial reviewer a second time. Decide at planning which fields are structured enough for scripts to verify and which require human evidence; do not claim complete automation of judgement.
done_when: On a fixture plan with three mandatory outcomes (add new behavior, remove an obsolete route, and complete the final review), plan validation produces a requirement-to-check map with positive and negative checks; a build that leaves any one outcome unproved, skipped, stale for current HEAD, or justified only by a Ruling cannot reach STEP 9's first push or an existing-PR push; a user-approved plan revision and passing evidence for every requirement allow publication, while the ledger still records the deviation and 0015B owns the separate PR review/fix document.

comments.content: Dropped by Maicon on 2026-10-09 (board review): more ceremony in the internal pipeline. The done gates, the test-loss guard and CI already cover most of it.

title: Ferramenta interna: preview no /board do diff que a ativação de features e plugins injeta na instalação do usuário
tldr: Ferramenta interna do gestor do codeadd: expandir o /board (habilitado no `npm run setup`) para simular a ativação de cada feature e plugin e mostrar o diff real que a instalação do usuário produz. Nada muda para quem instala o framework — é transparente.
notes: Pedido do usuario: uma forma visual de analisar internamente o que cada feature, plugin e qualquer coisa que altera prompts/instruções faz na instalação. Poder simular a ativação de uma feature (exemplo) e ver um diff das modificações que serão aplicadas no framework do usuario.

O motor já é puro, o que torna o preview barato: `applyInjectionToContent(content, points, sections, provider)` em `cli/src/injection-core.js:214` recebe o conteúdo do arquivo como string e devolve `{content, missed}` sem tocar no disco. Um preview é carregar o arquivo, rodar essa função com os pontos/fragmentos da feature e comparar entrada e saída. `enableFeature`/`disableFeature` (`cli/src/features.js:172`/`:213`) são esse mesmo caminho, mas escrevem.

O que alimenta o preview: o sidecar `.codeadd/injection-points.json` (emitido pelo build, `extractInjectionPoints` em `scripts/build.js`) dá os anchors por namespace/name/resource; os fragmentos vêm de `.codeadd/fragments/<feature>/<command>.md` (features) e `.codeadd/plugins/<plugin>/fragments/**` (plugins). Registries: `FEATURES` em `cli/src/features.js` (tdd-pipeline, qa-pipeline, docs-pruning, board) e `cli/src/plugins.json` + `cli/src/plugins.js`.

Plugins têm duas pernas: fragmentos em comandos e fragmentos por-agente (`getAgentFragments`/`injectAgentFragments`, `cli/src/injection-core.js:397`/`:419`) — o preview precisa cobrir as duas, senão esconde metade do efeito. O provedor também conta: `resolveResourceTargets` mapeia um recurso lógico para cada provedor selecionado e `resolvePlaceholders` resolve `{{cmd:}}`/`{{skill:}}` por provedor, então o mesmo fragmento pode dar diffs diferentes por provedor.

Decidir a superfície: (a) subcomando CLI `codeadd features preview [--all|--feature X]` que imprime um diff unificado e/ou escreve os arquivos resultantes num diretório temporário; (b) uma tela no board, hoje `board/server.mjs` (read-only, servido em 127.0.0.1, cabeçalho já reserva endpoints `/api/runs`); (c) as duas sobre uma implementação só — o board lê via API e a CLI imprime. A prova tem que ser a mesma nos dois lados.

Pergunta de escopo obrigatória: diff contra o quê? contra o arquivo instalado atual (mostra o que ligar muda agora) ou contra o comando base sem nenhuma feature (mostra o efeito isolado de cada uma)? Provavelmente o segundo para comparar features e o primeiro para ver o estado alvo. Registrar qual é o padrão e permitir o outro.

Armadilha de ordenação já registrada: quando duas features dividem o mesmo anchor, a ordem de injeção depende de qual foi ligada por último (ver 0007B). Um preview que não usar ordem determinística mostra um diff que não é o que a instalação produz.

Relação com 0014B (fallback de fragmento) e 0013B (docs de feature determinísticos + API/MCP): este ticket é sobre VER o efeito; 0014B muda o que é injetado e 0013B é sobre os docs de feature do projeto do usuário. Não duplicar. Quando 0014B entrar, o preview precisa mostrar o fallback também.

ESCOPO TRAVADO (2026-09-27) — a ferramenta é TOTALMENTE INTERNA. Quem instala o framework nao ganha nada disso; e transparente. Ela serve ao gestor do codeadd, que precisa analisar o diff de cada feature/plugin como se estivesse sendo ativado na maquina de um usuario do codeadd. O layer do ticket passa a ser `internal`.

Onde ela mora: o frontend do `/board`, que deixa de ser so um board e ganha a tela de preview. Hoje `board/server.mjs` sobe read-only em 127.0.0.1 e `npm run board` (`package.json:9`) passa `--layers`. O `--layers` e exatamente o padrao de recurso INTERNO: `board/server.mjs:13` diz 'Off by default' e `board/server.mjs:196` so expoe o chip product/internal/both quando o flag esta ligado. O preview interno deve seguir esse mesmo padrao — so existe com o flag interno.

Como liga: a instalacao interna e o `npm run setup` (`package.json:5` = `node scripts/build-workbench.js && npm run build:board`). E o setup que compila o workbench e o board neste repo. O preview interno entra por esse caminho, nunca pelo build do produto nem pelo pacote npm (`release.yml` nao roda o setup).

Por que nao pode ser product: o board distribuido ao usuario (release asset instalado sob `.codeadd/board/`) nao pode ganhar a tela de preview, senao deixa de ser transparente. Se a tela compartilhar componentes com o board distribuido, o gate tem que garantir que ela so aparece com o flag interno ligado.

O que a ferramenta le para montar o diff: o codigo de injecao do produto (`cli/src/injection-core.js`) e o source/sidecar do produto (`framwork/.codeadd/injection-points.json`, `framwork/.codeadd/fragments`, `framwork/.codeadd/plugins`). Ela LE o produto, mas NAO muda o que o produto instala. Reusa a engine pura `applyInjectionToContent`, sem escrever no projeto.
done_when: Simular a ativação de uma feature (ex.: tdd-pipeline) e de um plugin (ex.: gitnexus) mostra, sem escrever nada no projeto, um diff por arquivo e por provedor das linhas que a instalação injetaria, igual ao diff que `codeadd features enable` produz de fato; ligar duas features que dividem um anchor mostra a mesma ordem determinística que a instalação real; e o mesmo efeito aparece na superfície escolhida (CLI e/ou board) a partir de uma implementação só.

tldr: Após o relatório completo, comandos manuais com próxima atividade oferecem instruções copiáveis em um único bloco, sem arquivo de handoff nem execução ao aceitar.
notes: Pedido: incluir no final de cada comando a criação de um arquivo com instruções para a próxima execução. Entregar ao usuário o comando e o caminho relativo direto do arquivo, prontos para copiar.

Reusar o padrão de timestamp já empregado no brainstorm: YYYY-MM-DDTHHMMSS-<slug>.md. O padrão foi encontrado em workbench/skills/add-framework--brainstorm/SKILL.md; isso é referência de nomenclatura, não pedido para alterar o pipeline interno.

Exemplo real fornecido pelo usuário: uma review-003 de outra aplicação libera correções de AUD-F01 a AUD-F04, consolida QA-F01/QA-F02 e registra AUD-F05 como disputed e QA-F03 como encerrado. Preservar trabalho de outras sessões, revalidar findings contra o código atual, evitar reaplicar patches e manter histórico de Ruling, Resolution Annex e evidências. Indicar restrição de QA à feature e criação de nova run sem sobrescrever evidência anterior quando aplicável.

Resolver no desenho como comandos sem feature ainda criada, como brainstorm, e comandos sem próxima ação atendem ao pedido de cada comando. Não inventar uma feature só para guardar o prompt. Definir também a forma de consumir o arquivo na próxima invocação e evitar que o prompt se torne uma segunda fonte de verdade divergente da review/plano.

R3: recusa não gera bloco nem execução. R8: todos os finishing commands têm cobertura de contrato, build/graph/regressão e conversas reais. O desenho persistido original foi explicitamente substituído pelo usuário pelo desenho chat-only.

title: Diagnosticar e corrigir ERROR=node-missing nos scripts do board em Bash non-login no Windows/WSL
tldr: Evitar que a resolução do Node bloqueie leitura e escrita do backlog sem uma orientação clara quando Bash non-login não encontra o runtime.
notes: Reproduzido nesta sessão: bash framwork/.codeadd/scripts/backlog.sh list --all retorna ERROR=node-missing e exit 2. Com bash -lc, a leitura funciona e retorna os 17 tickets existentes.

Falha confirmada antes da execução do CLI: backlog.sh:36 exige command -v node. Reexecutar a mesma guarda em Bash non-login imprime GUARD-FAILED. Não há evidência de defeito em backlog-cli.cjs, no formato do board ou no frontend.

Ambiente observado: PowerShell no Windows; bash executa WSL2 Debian 13. O Windows tem C:/nvm4w/nodejs/node.exe v24.11.0; no WSL command -v node.exe encontra /mnt/c/nvm4w/nodejs/node.exe e node.exe -v funciona. Bash login encontra /home/fnd/.local/bin/node v22.20.0.

A profile Linux contém inclusão de $HOME/.local/bin no PATH. A diferença login/non-login está confirmada pela guarda e pela leitura; algumas sondagens de PATH e exit code produziram saída contraditória via PowerShell, então confirmar a inicialização do ambiente ao implementar em vez de tratar cada sonda como prova conclusiva.

backlog-commit.sh:135 chama backlog.sh e herda a dependência de resolução do Node. Isso pode bloquear os modos de escrita também; não foi tentada uma escrita pelo ambiente que falha. delivered.sh:86 tem guarda idêntica.
Workaround validado para leitura: iniciar Bash como login shell. A escrita desta captura será executada com o mesmo ambiente; isso não altera os scripts.

Escolher uma solução compatível com o contrato bash 3.2+ e node >=18: resolução/invocação do runtime ou orientação explícita de ambiente. Não aceitar node.exe sem verificar caminhos POSIX, cwd e operações completas de escrita em WSL.

Quando Node estiver realmente ausente, manter erro de dependência claro. Acrescentar diagnóstico acionável que distinga ambiente do Bash, Node Windows e Node Linux. Cobrir os casos relevantes nos testes dos scripts.
done_when: Reproduzir em Windows/WSL Bash non-login com Node Linux disponível apenas no ambiente login e com node.exe acessível; verificar a solução escolhida para list/search e escrita por backlog-commit.sh em repositório descartável, incluindo caminhos/cwd; verificar Linux com node normal e Node realmente ausente; testes documentam os resultados e o erro orienta como corrigir o ambiente sem atribuir a falha ao parsing do board.

title: Listagem do backlog para o agente enxuta (id, status, titulo, tldr), e o registro completo só num get detalhado
tldr: A leitura da lista do backlog volta enxuta — o agente identifica qual ticket é o do pedido pelo título e pelo tldr, e só abre o ticket inteiro quando precisar do resto.
notes: Pedido do usuário: a listagem de backlog lida pelo agente deve voltar simplificada — mais ou menos título e tldr — e a informação completa deve ficar num get detalhado.

MEDIÇÃO (2026-10-04, `list --all` com 21 tickets, 76.904 bytes no total): `notes` 52.624 bytes (68,4%), `done_when` 7.952 (10,3%), `paths` 4.024 (5,2%), `tldr` 5.004 (6,5%), `title` 1.752 (2,3%), todos os outros campos juntos ~1.500 (2%). Some ~4KB de overhead não contido nessa tabela: 21 linhas repetindo os nomes de todas as chaves e a pontuação do JSON.

Consequência da medição: `notes` + `done_when` + `paths` são 83,9% do peso. Tirando os três, a lista cai de 76,9KB para ~12,2KB. Tirando também o repetidor de chaves e cortando o tldr, ela chega perto de 5KB — cerca de 15 vezes menor.

Causa exata: `renderOperation` em `framwork/.codeadd/scripts/backlog-cli.cjs:202` empurra a linha verbatim (`out.push(row)`, linha 215) — o JSONL cru e completo, `notes` incluído, em toda leitura. A forma simplificada é decisão da camada de stdout do CLI, não do core: o core devolve o registro e o CLI decide o que imprime.

⛔ O get detalhado NÃO existe hoje. MODES em `framwork/.codeadd/scripts/backlog-cli.cjs:46` é `['add','update','comment','move','remove','list','search']`. Criar um modo é decisão de desenho, não detalhe de implementação.

⚠️ PRECEDENTE CONTRÁRIO, já registrado: a entrega `2026-09-20T222814-PLAN--project-backlog-skill-lifecycle-and-rename` gravou na ledger (F5, `ledger.md:19`) que um ticket é lido por id através de `backlog.sh list --all` filtrado em `\"id\":\"<id>\"`, e NÃO por um get-by-id novo — porque `search` nunca casa o id e adicionar um modo reabriria o subtopic 001, que uma Global Constraint proíbe. Este ticket contraria esse ruling de propósito, por pedido do usuário. A saída mais barata está no item seguinte.

DECISÃO A DECIDIR PRIMEIRO — fazer `search` casar o id. Medido: `search 0020B` devolve TICKETS_RETURNED=0. Documentado em `add--doc-schemas/references/backlog.md`: `search` casa `title`, `tldr` e `notes`, nunca o id (e `labels` é explicitamente só para filtrar). Se `search` casar o id, `search <id>` já entrega o ticket inteiro sem criar modo novo — e portanto sem reabrir o subtopic 001, que foi exatamente o motivo do ruling F5. Se isso bastar, o modo `get` nem precisa existir; se não bastar, aí sim criar `get <id>`, com o ruling F5 explicitamente reaberto no desenho.

CAMPOS DA LISTAGEM, e por que cada um. `status` é obrigatório: custa 126 bytes para 21 tickets (0,2% do total) e 5 dos 21 estão `done` — sem ele o agente resolve o pedido para um ticket já entregue. `work_id` como flag de um caractere: só 3 de 21 têm plano em andamento, e diz que alguém já pegou esse. `updated_at` só como data (10 caracteres): `created_at` pode sair, é quase sempre igual ao `updated_at` neste board. `theme`: 16 bytes por ticket, preenchido em 20 de 21, agrupa o board de graça. `labels` (a layer): fica mais importante justamente porque `paths` sai da lista, então o label passa a ser o único sinal de product/internal/both. Opcional: a contagem de notes como aviso de profundidade antes de abrir o ticket. Fora da lista: `notes`, `done_when`, `paths`, `created_at`, `grounded` (true em 20 de 21, é ruído), `feature` (null nos 21) e `comments` (vazio nos 21).

TETO NO TLDR dentro da lista: o tldr já é comprido — média de 235 caracteres, e o maior tem 508 (0011B). Se a lista trouxer o tldr inteiro, ela continua grande. Cortar em ~120 caracteres na lista e deixar o texto inteiro no get.

CONTAGEM POR STATUS NO CABEÇALHO: hoje o cabeçalho só traz `BACKLOG_PRESENT`, `TICKETS_TOTAL`, `TICKETS_RETURNED` e `DAMAGED_LINES`. Acrescentar `STATUS_open=16`, `STATUS_done=5` entrega a forma do board em 5 linhas, antes de qualquer ticket. É o item mais barato da lista inteira.

PADRÃO ENXUTO, COMPLETO ATRÁS DE FLAG: o padrão passa a ser a linha enxuta e o registro completo sai por `--full`. O caminho inverso — padrão completo e linha enxuta atrás de flag — não resolve, porque o agente usa o padrão.
`list --ids`: só os ids na ordem de prioridade, ~150 bytes para o board inteiro. Responde 'o que tem no board' e é o que o `move --after <id>` precisa para resolver a âncora.
ESCALAR A LEITURA NO STEP 2 do comando interno: ler primeiro a lista enxuta dos tickets abertos, e só reler com `--all` quando o match falhar. 24% do board é `done` e quase nunca é o alvo.

TIRAR A REPETIÇÃO DAS CHAVES JSON: são ~4KB de overhead puro (21 linhas × nomes de chave e pontuação). Uma linha por ticket em colunas fixas economiza isso e é mais fácil de varrer. Quebra o `grep '"id":"<id>"'`, que hoje é usado só por `board/test/native-backlog.test.ts`, `board/e2e/native-backlog.spec.ts` e `workbench/commands/add-framework--backlog.md` — decidir o que cada um passa a ler, em vez de deixar quebrar.
REGRA A ESCREVER NO DESENHO, senão o próximo autor volta a adicionar campo: a listagem nunca carrega `notes`, `done_when` nem `paths`.

O board NÃO é afetado: `board/server.mjs:83` importa `executeBacklog` direto do core gerado (`runtime/backlog-core.cjs`) e monta os tickets ele mesmo (`server.mjs:92`, mode list, filter `*`). A UI nunca passa pela stdout do CLI, então a simplificação é só para o agente e o board continua vendo o registro inteiro.

Quem consome a listagem hoje (grep por `list --all` e pelo nome da CLI): `workbench/commands/add-framework--backlog.md` (STEP 1 na íntegra, e `search` no STEP 2), `workbench/skills/add-plan-authoring/SKILL.md:264`, o skill de produto `add--backlog`, e os testes `board/test/native-backlog.test.ts:15` e `board/e2e/native-backlog.spec.ts:14`, que chamam a CLI.

`framwork/.codeadd/skills/add--doc-schemas/references/backlog.md` é o dono dos campos e das chaves: a linha dos modos read (`list`, `search`), as regras de leitura (`list` tem default open; `--all`; `--status <nome>`; `search` casa title, tldr e notes e mantém a ordem do board, que é a ordem de prioridade) e o vocabulário de `REFUSED=`. Modo novo e forma nova de saída entram ali, não só no script.

Relação com 0009B (nunca passar corpo multilinha inline): ali o ponto é a escrita do registro, que viaja por `--record-file` em vez de heredoc. Não duplicar aquela regra. Aqui o alvo é o custo de leitura da listagem.
done_when: `list --all` num board com 21 tickets imprime uma linha enxuta por ticket contendo id, status, title e tldr com teto de ~120 caracteres, sem `notes`, `done_when` nem `paths`, e cabe em menos de um sexto do tamanho medido hoje (76.904 bytes); o cabeçalho traz a contagem por status (`STATUS_open=`, `STATUS_done=`); `list --ids` devolve os ids na ordem de prioridade; `--full` devolve o registro completo; `search <id>` casa o id (hoje devolve TICKETS_RETURNED=0) e, se essa via não bastar, existe `get <id>` com o registro inteiro e o ruling F5 reaberto de forma explícita; o STEP 1 do `add-framework--backlog` roda a lista enxuta e o STEP 2 escala para `--all` só quando o match falhar; `cli/tests/backlog-cli.test.js` e `framwork/.codeadd/scripts/tests/backlog.bats` cobrem a linha enxuta, o teto do tldr, a ausência de notes, o `--full` e o `--ids`; e o board continua exibindo o registro inteiro, porque não consome a stdout da CLI.

title: Corrigir consulta ao histórico de entregas via graph.js no Windows/WSL após migração nativa do backlog
tldr: Fazer a consulta ao histórico de entregas funcionar no Windows/WSL sem depender de caminhos Windows aceitos pelo Bash ou do Node disponível apenas em login shell, e expor diagnóstico útil quando falhar.
notes: Ocorrido em 2026-10-04 durante o brainstorm do ticket 0018B. A consulta node scripts/graph.js history add-review retornou history unavailable for product/command/add-review: read-failed (delivered.sh exited 127). O brainstorm continuou com histórico NOT VERIFIED. A falha é na consulta ao delivery index, não na leitura de tickets nem no frontend do board.

Reprodução direta pelo mesmo spawnSync de scripts/graph.js: bash recebe C:\github\xmaiconx\code-addiction\framwork\.codeadd\scripts\delivered.sh; status=127, stdout vazio, stderr=/bin/bash: C:githubxmaiconxcode-addictionframwork.codeaddscriptsdelivered.sh: No such file or directory. O script não chegou a executar nessa chamada. A ponte Windows/WSL não preserva/resolve o caminho Windows fornecido.

Segundo problema confirmado separadamente: spawnSync('bash', ['framwork/.codeadd/scripts/delivered.sh','read','add-review','--limit','50']) encontra o script, mas retorna status=2 e ERROR=node-missing. delivered.sh:86 exige command -v node em Bash non-login.

Controle positivo: spawnSync('bash', ['-lc','bash framwork/.codeadd/scripts/delivered.sh read add-review --limit 50']) retorna status=0, MATCHED_LIVE=3, MATCHED_DEAD=0 e três registros. O índice está legível nesse ambiente. Este controle é diagnóstico, não uma correção aplicada.

Relação com 0019B, já done sob work_id 2026-10-04T004044-PLAN--native-node-backlog: a leitura node framwork/.codeadd/scripts/backlog-cli.cjs list --all funcionou nesta sessão, retornando 19 tickets. A migração nativa do backlog não eliminou a dependência de Bash na consulta do delivery index. Não reabrir 0019B nem atribuir este erro ao parser do backlog sem evidência.

scripts/graph.js:285-301 mantém DELIVERED_SH absoluto e spawnSync(bash, args). Em status não zero, linhas 311-314 preservam somente uma linha ERROR= ou o exit code, descartando o stderr que nesta reprodução revela o caminho inválido. A mensagem resumida ocultou a causa real.

mcp/engine.mjs também delega history e touched_by ao delivered.sh por spawnSync; mcp/server.mjs declara history sobre essa superfície. O padrão compartilhado precisa ser inspecionado e coberto, mas a reprodução executada nesta sessão foi a CLI graph.js, não o MCP.

A chamada original incluiu vários nomes depois de history; a CLI usa um alvo posicional. As reproduções isoladas com add-review confirmam a falha independentemente disso. Consultar cada artefacto separadamente no diagnóstico/validação.

Preservar um único proprietário do formato delivery index e a equivalência CLI/MCP; não resolver com um segundo parser improvisado. Escolher solução portátil para invocação/delegação e manter diagnóstico acionável de runtime/caminho. Não alterar código nesta captura.
done_when: No Windows/PowerShell com Bash WSL non-login, node scripts/graph.js history add-review lê o índice sem erro de caminho ou Node; a superfície MCP equivalente retorna o mesmo resultado e touched_by é verificado quando usa a mesma ponte. Testes reproduzem caminho Windows, runtime fora do PATH non-login, Linux normal e dependências ausentes; stderr/diagnóstico distingue falha antes de abrir o script de ERROR=node-missing. Leitura e publicação nativas do backlog permanecem funcionais e nenhum segundo parser do delivery index é introduzido.

Em `add--ecosystem/SKILL.md:290` a linha de `backlog.sh` traz a descrição completa ('the seven local modes', 'Runs no git command at all'); a de `backlog-cli.cjs` (linha 291) é só 'the native local entry'. E em `add--backlog/SKILL.md:9-12` o bloco `uses:` declara os QUATRO: `backlog-cli.cjs`, `backlog-commit.cjs`, `backlog.sh` e `backlog-commit.sh`. CAUSA 3 — Seis lugares dizem que ele ainda funciona. `add--backlog/SKILL.md:70-72`, `add--doc-schemas/references/backlog.md:8` e `:262`, `add--resource-path-convention/SKILL.md:86`, `workbench/skills/add-plan-authoring/SKILL.md:300`, `workbench/commands/add-framework--backlog.md:202`. CAUSA 4 — O guard do wrapper é literalmente o mesmo que este ticket e 0019B descrevem. `backlog.sh:42` e `backlog-commit.sh:43` são `command -v node`; `delivered.sh:86` é idêntico. Isso depende de Bash login. Neste repositório o agente roda em PowerShell, o `bash` é WSL2 non-login, e o Node Linux só entra pelo profile de login (`$HOME/.local/bin`). title: Migrar os scripts .sh restantes para Node, para que bash deixe de ser um requisito do pipeline
tldr: Cada script .sh que o pipeline ainda chama em Bash vira um módulo Node chamado por nome, para que nenhuma rota do framework dependa de um shell resolver runtime — e para que o Windows funcione sem login shell, sem WSL e sem ponte de caminho.
notes: Pedido do usuário em 2026-10-04, durante o close-out da entrega compact-backlog-reads: dois problemas实践中 do mesmo dia (ERROR=node-missing em Bash non-login e ERROR=not-a-git-repository numa worktree Windows)-aboutem o mesmo nó — o pipeline reaching por bash um runtime que nem todo shell resolve. Migrar para Node remove a classe pela raiz em vez de consertar ponte por ponte.

O que existe hoje: 19 .sh em framwork/.codeadd/scripts/ (build-ledger, build-setup, converge-gates, delivered, done, get-branch-metadata, get-main-branch, hotfix-gates, init, log-iteration, log-jsonl, migrate-context-files, migrate-ids, next-id, qa-evidence, qa-preflight, review-package, status, task-brief) e 3 em scripts/ (create-release-tag, release, smoke-test). O backlog já provou que a migração funciona e o padrão: backlog.sh/backlog-commit.sh foram removidos pelo predecessor 2026-10-04T181131-PLAN--remove-backlog-shell-wrappers, e os seis CJS canônicos ficaram como única entrada, com as suítes Bats preservadas chamando Node diretamente.

O caso mais caro é delivered.sh: ele é o dono do formato do delivery index, alcançado por spawnSync('bash') em scripts/graph.js e em mcp/engine.mjs. Enquanto ele for Bash, o close-out de uma entrega em worktree Windows não tem rota, e o histórico de entregas responde NOT VERIFIED na plataforma onde o usuário trabalha.

O caso、次: next-id.sh e status.sh mantêm a regra NEXT_ID_AGREE entre dois calculadores que reimplementam a mesma varredura em Bash. O allocator já é nativo (backlog-id.cjs); os dois Bash são agora uma segunda e uma terceira implementação do mesmo cálculo, cada uma com sua própria suíte. Consolidar em Node remove a classe inteira de divergência entre calculadores.

A ordem proposta: delivered.sh primeiro (destrava o índice de entregas e o histórico), depois next-id.sh + status.sh (uma implementação do allocator em vez de três), depois o restante por ondas cada uma com a suíte Bats correspondente portada antes da remoção — a regra do predecessor: preservar os casos comportamentais, trocar apenas o transporte, e nunca apagar um teste de negócio junto com a casca que o executava.

Restrições que a miguração tem de respeitar: scripts/ e AGENTS.md são internos; framwork/.codeadd/scripts/ é product e cada script é distribuído verbatim; o release.sh continua sendo o único caminho de release e roda a partir de worktree; nenhuma receita de produto pode voltar a nomear `bash .codeadd/scripts/...` como caminho suportado. Um .sh que não é chamado por nenhum artefacto ativo não precisa de equivalente — some com o gate de inventário, como aconteceu com os dois wrappers.

Relacionado: 0021B (o defeito de ponte observado hoje) e 0019B (done, diagnóstico do runtime). Este ticket não fecha 0021B por decisão própria — o leitor nativo que os dois compartilham é o que fecha.
done_when: Nenhum comando, skill, agente ou script do repositório executa um .sh: `grep -rn "bash .codeadd/scripts" framwork/.codeadd workbench` e `grep -rn "\.sh\b" scripts/*.js` não retornam nenhuma chamada ativa; cada .sh removido tem suíte Bats portada para o módulo Node correspondente com os mesmos casos (verificado por relatório de caso preservado/substituído/exclusivo), exatamente como o predecessor fez com backlog.bats; delivered.sh tem equivalente Node e scripts/graph.js e mcp/engine.mjs o alcançam sem spawn de shell, com `node scripts/graph.js history <artefact>` respondendo no Windows sem login shell e dentro de uma worktree; next-id.sh e status.sh convergem para uma implementação Node única e NEXT_ID_AGREE passa a comparar Node contra Node; e `npm test`, `npm run test:scripts` e `npm run release` passam numa máquina Windows sem Git-Bash e sem WSL no caminho.

title: Lighter product add-build: cut repeated review and validation dispatches
tldr: Users report development got slow; the build repeats reviewer, readback and test dispatches. Cut them without changing what gets checked.
notes: Analysis 2026-10-08: a typical 2-area build has about 10 review and test dispatches, the worst case passes 20, and TASKS MODE passes 40.

(1) In TASKS MODE run the validator reviewer once per area, after its last task, not once per task. Commits stay per task, with the build as the commit gate (add-build.md COMMIT CONTRACT today ties the commit to the area validator returning).
(2) Remove the readback-agent dispatch from add-build entirely (frontmatter `agent: readback-agent`, the readback step and the `Readback:` ledger lines). The readback at the end of add-plan stays.
(3) A fix round whose routed rows come only from build errors or test-agent BLOCKED gets no re-review. Its gate is build and tests going green, and the Final Review reads that fix diff.

(4) add-review does not repeat what the build Final Review already did (OWASP, spec audit) when the ledger has a passing Final review and no commit after it. add-build stops suggesting add-review as the next step.
Keep fix attempts at 3.
Check add--review-discipline for the per-command dispatch counts it states, and keep them consistent.
done_when: add-build.md dispatches the validator once per area in TASKS MODE, has no readback-agent dispatch, skips re-review for build-error/BLOCKED-only fix rounds, and no longer suggests add-review as next step; add-review skips OWASP and spec audit when the ledger has a passing Final review with no later commit; fix attempts remain 3; npm test passes.

title: Non-interactive installer: install, modify and update run from flags, with no prompts
tldr: A bot or assistant can install, update, and turn features, plugins and providers on or off from the command line, while the interactive flow for humans stays the same.
notes: Requested by Maicon on 2026-10-09.
Builds on 0027B, which only made install exit with an error when there is no TTY. This ticket replaces that dead end with a real non-interactive path.

Flags: --providers is required without a TTY (none = only the core). --enable-feature / --disable-feature and --enable-plugin / --disable-plugin are deltas in install and modify. In modify, --providers is the final set. Scope stays --global / --user. Confirmation is --force. Non-interactive mode is detected by !stdin.isTTY, with no yes flag.
With the flags given, no prompt appears. Missing required input in non-interactive mode fails with a clear error, never a hang.
The interactive flow is unchanged when the flags are absent.
Document the flags in the agent-mode guide so bots know how to call them.
Shaped with Maicon on 2026-10-09 by Code Addiction PM; intent decided: no reinstall flag, features list prints without a TTY, uninstall with both scopes and --json are out of scope.
done_when: With stdin not a TTY, install (with --providers and feature flags), modify (with flags and --force) and update finish without a prompt and change providers, features and plugins as asked; missing --providers or a destructive step without --force exits 1 with a clear message; features list prints and exits; tests cover each case, codeadd --help and the agent-mode guide list the flags, and the interactive flow is unchanged.
